entries.label: Unhackable internet
key_players: University of Science and Technology of China
entries.quote: The internet is increasingly vulnerable to hacking; a quantum one would be unhackable.

entries.label: Hyper-personalized medicine
entries.quote: Genetic medicine tailored to a single patient means hope for people whose ailments were previously uncurable.

entries.label: Digital money
entries.quote: As the use of physical cash declines, so does the freedom to transact without an intermediary.

entries.label: Anti-aging drugs
entries.quote: A number of different diseases, including cancer, heart disease, and dementia, could potentially be treated by slowing aging.

entries.label: AI-discovered molecules
entries.quote: Commercializing a new drug costs around $2.5 billion on average. One reason is the difficulty of finding promising molecules.

entries.label: Satellite mega-constellations
entries.quote: These systems can blanket the globe with high-speed internet—or turn Earth's orbit into a junk-ridden minefield.

entries.label: Quantum supremacy
entries.quote: Eventually, quantum computers will be able to solve problems no classical machine can manage.

entries.label: Tiny AI
entries.quote: Our devices no longer need to talk to the cloud for us to benefit from the latest AI-driven features.

entries.label: Differential privacy
entries.availability: Its use in the 2020 US Census will be the biggest-scale application yet
entries.quote: It is increasingly difficult for the US Census Bureau to keep the data it collects private.

entries.label: Climate change attribution
key_players: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
entries.quote: It's providing a clearer sense of how climate change is worsening the weather, and what we'll need to do to prepare.

notes: Ten entries. Quote is the 'Why it matters' line. Every entry has an availability statement; some are not time bands ('This year', a census event).
